FAIRNESS FIX: the On-Chain tab of ProvablyFairVerifier hardcoded valid:true and reported "verified" for ANY input (wrong block hash included), computing plain SHA-256 while its comment claimed keccak256. Authoritative chain algorithm is HMAC-SHA512 domain-separated + length-prefixed over clientSeed/betAmount/gameType/paramBlob/decidingHash/betID with roll=scaleRange(OutcomeToScaled(entropy 0:8),10000) - even the keeper PlayResponse doc misstates it. serverSeed/paramBlob/decidingHash never reach the client so no in-browser recompute can be truthful; panel now publishes the real algorithm + on-chain coordinates, informational styling, no fabricated roll. CROSS-FILE NODE-ID COLLISION, not a dice screen - deferred and flagged rather than built. This id sits in dice.nodes.txt at line 3, wedged between 2713-3937 (Directory), 2713-3943 (Breakpoint), 2738-28626 (Rectangle 147) and two more Breakpoints - i.e. surrounded entirely by Skai-Games canvas furniture - yet dice.titles.tsv gives it the title 'Skai > Home > Add > upload image > conversation 4 1VH (1440 x 900px)', and the SAME bare id appears in home.nodes.txt line 348 with the identical title. So the TITLE is Skai-Web-App's and cannot be trusted to describe whatever Skai-Games node carries this id; on its neighbours' evidence that node is more canvas furniture. Deliberately NOT deleted from dice.nodes.txt - removing a node id is a structural catalog edit that could hide a real frame, and the honest record is that this entry's title is unreliable. It is the ONLY dice frame with no verdict, and it is a cataloguing artifact rather than unbuilt dice work, so it does not hold the family open. Worth a titles re-harvest against M6r9FEn042UWTQD1zvy6GM to settle what the Skai-Games node actually is.
